description: This USDA Climate Hubs series presents farm case studies in which producers used the Adaptation Resources for Agriculture framework to identify climate change impacts, challenges and opportunities on their land and to choose farm-level adaptation tactics for extreme and uncertain conditions. The ten studies listed include an artisan cider apple orchard and an organic dairy in Wisconsin, farms in Texas, south-east Indiana and Colorado, two Alaska farms, a farm in Puerto Rico, a poultry and beef farm in south-eastern Mississippi and a farm in Arkansas. It is published by the USDA Climate Hubs. The framework's menu of strategies was written for the Midwest and Northeast, with companion material for Alaska and California specialty crops, but the cases span US regions. The studies, the downloadable workbook and a training webinar are free online; the page states no licence, as usual for US Government works. Caveats: each study is a single-farm planning exercise, so results are qualitative and not a sample of US agriculture, and the page read gives no dates. For simulation it offers documented adaptation choices that can inform farm-level scenarios in food system resilience models, such as irrigation, crop or livestock changes after drought or heat. It is related to the NAP-Ag country case study series record in this catalogue, which covers national adaptation planning for agriculture.
